description: Connected part of the W_lambda-weighted nuclear-braid standard-rep transfer-matrix product for 2H/3He/3H/4He/6Li/12C: localizes the extensive binding channel to the non-abelian (2,1) rep (C_std=0 at A=2, grows with bonds for A>=3). Mechanism probe; NOT a binding closure; no fit.

assertions.name: connected_channel_nonempty_A3plus
assertions.detail: |C_std|>0 for all A>=3 [0.461, 0.304, 1.005, 0.531, 1.216] (extensive channel NON-EMPTY, localized to std (2,1) rep)

assertions.name: extensive_piece_in_nonabelian_std_channel
assertions.detail: 4He: W_(2,1)*C_std=0.66430 (connected, non-abelian) vs 1-dim factorized parts 0.33395 — extensive binding is the std connected part

result.verdict: MECHANISM LOCALIZED (no closure): the extensive/connected binding channel is the STANDARD (2,1) rep — the non-abelian transfer-matrix product over inter-nucleon bonds — whose connected part C_std vanishes for A=2 and is NON-EMPTY (>0) for A>=3. The 1-dim (sym/alt) reps factorize over bonds and are disconnected/intensive. This is the (2,1) channel that brackets the deuteron f_pn (#2528). HONEST CAVEAT: C_std is NON-MONOTONE in bond count and its per-bond value SHRINKS for heavy nuclei — the fixed-H_3 braid localizes the channel but does not by itself sustain extensivity past the light nuclei (consistent with the known r18k det-direction non-monotonicity + light-nuclei breakdown). Localizes/confirms the channel is non-empty; does NOT set a scale, land AME magnitudes, or wire anything. No fit.

context.structural: 1-dim reps factorize (disconnected); (2,1) is the non-abelian transfer-matrix product (connected)
context.scope: mechanism localization; NOT a closure; no scale/wiring/fit
